chapter: Growing up: theaters and the lakefront
title: Spanish Fort concert band and teacher Armin Vesey
summary: As a child of ten or twelve Hirsch went with his father to hear the concert band at Spanish Fort and talks about Armin Vesey and his trumpet teaching.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the first horn: clarinet and saxophone beginnings

blocks.x: Did you ever go out to the lakefront when you were a kid? To hear music?

I used to go when I was a child. Maybe 10 or 12 years old when my daddy played out at Spanish Fort. In the afternoon, they used to have a concert band. Pal Eddie was a conductor. Pil된 stuff with stuff

And I used to go out there with my father and hear them play the concert music. Was that the West End Band? No, that was Spanish Fort. That was Spanish Fort Band. There was a batch of bands my daddy was with. I mean, Armin Vesey was with his band. I don't know if you ever heard of Armin Vesey? Yeah. He was one of the teachers of, he taught everybody how to play. He had a style of teaching trumpet that you didn't pick up a trumpet until after you played with a mouthpiece for three months. He got the feel of a mouthpiece. Is that right? Armin Vesey, his son was Chester Vesey. You probably knew Chester.
No, there was another son I think I talked to.
He was a trumpet player. He was a cornetist.
Carondelet and Washington made it as guy.
Armin was not a great trumpet player but he was a section man. I mean, section, when I say section I mean a reader, not a faker.
Well, did they have any fakers out there? No?
